1. Policy Statement, Authority, and Supersession Notice

*** AUTHORITATIVE NOTICE: THIS IS THE CURRENT, AUTHORITATIVE REMOTE WORK POLICY ***
This document establishes the official and active Remote Work Policy Version 2.0 for Threshold Enterprise Systems,
effective January 1, 2025. THIS DOCUMENT FORMALLY SUPERSEDES REMOTE WORK POLICY VERSION 1.0
(DOCUMENT ID: HR-003) IN ITS ENTIRETY. All prior guidelines, remote day quotas, and legacy telecommuting
procedures under HR-003 are null and void.
Threshold Enterprise Systems embraces a modern, flexible hybrid work philosophy that combines the creative synergy of
in-person collaboration with the focused productivity of remote working. This policy outlines the operating rules, eligibility
standards, technological requirements, and behavioral expectations governing hybrid and remote arrangements across all
global business units.

2. Scope and Organizational Applicability

This policy applies to all full-time regular employees and eligible long-term contractors across all operating entities of
Threshold Enterprise Systems in India, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Singapore.
Hybrid remote arrangements are available to employees whose job functions can be effectively executed via modern
enterprise cloud tools, collaborative software repositories, and digital communication platforms without continuous on-site
presence.
Certain operational roles requiring physical presence (such as data center hardware technicians, physical security
personnel, and executive workplace hospitality teams) may be subject to localized on-site scheduling requirements as
designated by departmental leadership.

3. AUTHORITATIVE REMOTE WORK ALLOCATION: MAXIMUM 3 DAYS PER WEEK

UNDER THIS AUTHORITATIVE VERSION 2.0 POLICY, ELIGIBLE EMPLOYEES MAY WORK REMOTELY FOR A
MAXIMUM OF THREE (3) DAYS PER WEEK (60% REMOTE ALLOCATION).
Employees are required to work on-site at a designated corporate facility for a minimum of two (2) days per week. This
3-day remote / 2-day on-site balance represents our corporate standard designed to maintain strong cultural cohesion,
cross-functional collaboration, and high-performance delivery.

Teams are encouraged to coordinate designated 'In-Office Anchor Days' (e.g., Tuesdays and Thursdays) to maximize the
collaborative benefits of shared physical presence during design reviews, architectural planning, and team retrospectives.

4. Eligibility and Onboarding Period Requirements

All full-time employees who have completed an initial thirty (30) days of service and maintain a performance standing of
'Meets Expectations' or above are eligible to participate in the hybrid remote model.
During the initial thirty-day onboarding window, new hires are encouraged to spend three to four days per week in the office
to accelerate mentorship, team integration, and cultural orientation. Following this orientation period, the full 3-day remote
allowance becomes accessible upon manager confirmation in Workday.
Participation in remote work is a workplace privilege linked to demonstrated autonomy, dependable communication, and
consistent deliverable achievement. If an employee is placed on a formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP under
HR-006), their manager, in consultation with HR, may temporarily adjust their on-site requirements to provide direct
coaching.

5. Remote Work Request and Approval Process

Employees request their weekly hybrid schedule by submitting the 'Hybrid Working Agreement' in the Workday portal. The
submission identifies the employee's preferred remote days and in-office anchor days.
People Managers review and approve schedule submissions within five (5) business days. Approvals consider team
workload distribution, customer coverage across time zones, and project release milestones. Once approved, the schedule
is recorded in corporate team calendars.
Ad-hoc schedule modifications (such as swapping a remote day due to personal appointments or urgent on-site client visits)
may be coordinated directly with the manager via Slack or email without resubmitting the formal Workday agreement,
provided reasonable notice is given.

6. Information Security, Zero-Trust Architecture, and Data Handling

Remote work security operates under our enterprise Zero-Trust Security Framework. Employees are custodians of
proprietary data and must adhere strictly to information security mandates:

1. All corporate tasks must be executed exclusively on company-issued laptops enrolled in Enterprise Endpoint

Management with active endpoint detection and response (EDR).

2. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) via company-approved hardware security keys or authenticator apps is mandatory for

all resource access.

5. When working in public spaces or transit, privacy screens must be used, and voice discussions of proprietary algorithms,

7. Communication Expectations and Core Collaboration Hours

Maintaining effective asynchronous communication and rapid alignment across distributed teams is vital. Remote team
members are expected to observe Core Collaboration Hours from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM in their local office time zone.
Employees must maintain active status on enterprise messaging (Slack) during working hours, respond to direct inquiries in
a timely manner, and keep their Google/Outlook calendar current to reflect meeting availability, focus blocks, and lunch
periods.

Video presence is encouraged during interactive team rituals, client discussions, and 1-on-1 coaching meetings to foster
interpersonal connection, while respecting focus time and digital meeting fatigue.

8. Remote Workspace and Ergonomic Requirements

Employees are responsible for establishing a designated home working environment that supports productive, focused work
and professional confidentiality. The workspace should be quiet, well-lit, and ergonomically sound.
Threshold Enterprise Systems provides each eligible hybrid employee with an annual Home Office Stipend of $750 USD (or
local currency equivalent in INR, GBP, or SGD) to assist with ergonomic chairs, external monitors, keyboards, or
high-speed internet subsidies. Stipend claims are submitted through Concur with accompanying receipts.
The company does not assume liability for home utilities, homeowner insurance, or general household operating expenses
beyond the designated stipend.

9. Performance Expectations, Accountability, and Deliverables

Performance evaluation at Threshold Enterprise Systems is based strictly on measurable business outcomes, code quality,
customer satisfaction, project delivery, and adherence to company values—not physical seat time.
Remote team members are held to identical quality, velocity, and delivery standards as colleagues working on-site. Regular
bi-weekly 1-on-1 check-ins with people managers ensure clear alignment on OKRs, active sprint tasks, and long-term
career goals.
Failure to meet agreed deliverables or maintain professional responsiveness may result in a review of hybrid working
privileges in coordination with Human Resources.

10. Full-Time Remote Exceptions and Hardship Accommodations

Requests for full-time remote status (100% remote without on-site anchor days) or working remotely from a foreign
jurisdiction are exceptional and require formal review due to tax nexus, payroll compliance, and legal considerations.
An employee seeking a full-time remote exception or temporary medical accommodation must submit a formal application
through the HR Accommodation Portal. Endorsements are required from the Department Vice President, the Head of
Human Resources, and the Global Tax/Legal Director.
Temporary 'Work from Anywhere' provisions allow employees to work from an approved domestic or international location
for up to twenty (20) business days per calendar year, subject to manager pre-approval and compliance validation.

11. Policy Review, Administration, and Governance

This policy is owned and administered by the Human Resources Department in consultation with the Enterprise
Governance Committee and Information Security leadership. It is subject to bi-annual reviews to evaluate operational
efficacy, employee sentiment, and emerging collaborative technologies.
Any questions regarding the interpretation or practical application of Remote Work Policy Version 2.0 should be directed to
your departmental HR Business Partner or the HR Operations Helpdesk.
